text:
maya: Heads up — seeing massive local NVMe write latency on gpu-pool nodes (us-west-2). GPU pods are stalling and some OOM/killed. Not a kernel panic, looks IO-bound.

jordan: ugh. Any SMART or dmesg lines?

maya: quick paste from one affected host:```iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.00  9800.00  4096.00 245760.00   0.00   0.00    51.20   22.40  2.00   1.50    2.05   0.10  98.00
```

maya: also saw kernel messages about background scrub and 'nvme_admin_cmd' timeouts.

liam: so that's basically 98% util on nvme during background ops. Are we running the ephemeral-cleaner job concurrently with GPU jobs?

maya: yep — scheduled cron at 03:00 UTC, but spikes match the scrub window started by nvme-scrub.service — looks triggered by SMART threshold 0x08.

hao: can we throttle the scrub? which service is doing it — host OS or cloud agent?

anita: on these instances the cloud agent triggers vendor scrub when drive health degrades. We have a vendor ticket open for replacement but that'll take 36h to schedule.

jordan: short term: cordon affected nodes and drain GPU pods to avoid failed jobs. We should also reduce concurrency of ephemeral-cleaner and disable vendor scrub on that fleet until hardware replacement.

maya: creating a quick runbook: 1) cordon nodes with label gpu=true 2) drain non-critical pods 3) set ephemeral-cleaner concurrency=1 4) add CGroup blkiotune for scrub process to limit write_iops 5) open provider maintenance ticket

liam: samples of commands:```bash
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
# drain (preserve daemonsets)
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# reduce cleaner concurrency (ansible)
ansible -i inventory -m lineinfile -a "path=/etc/ephemeral-cleaner.conf regexp=^concurrency line='concurrency=1'" gpu-fleet
# throttle scrub (systemd scope)
systemd-run --scope -p IOWeight=10 -p CPUShares=50 /usr/bin/nvme-scrub
```

hao: we don't have IOWeight widely used — fallback: use ionice/blkio cgroups on the scrub process. I'll push a one-off systemd drop-in.

anita: I'll coordinate with provider for a swap. For now we should mark these nodes as 'reduced-capacity' in the autoscaler so new GPU jobs don't schedule there.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4839 "nvme background scrub causing high disk utilization on GPU nodes" — assigned to eng-infra. https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-4839

sre-bot: PagerDuty alert escalated to oncall@redwood at 1805123520.

jordan: quick performance note — enabling prefix/KV cache on model-serving might soften the impact while we move pods off. But main problem is write tail latency.

maya: rolling the plan now: cordoning 4 nodes (gpu-node-42..45), draining non-critical, reducing cleaner concurrency, adding systemd drop-in with ionice + blkio limits, and marking nodes in autoscaler.

liam: please add a short monitoring dashboard for NVMe %util and background-scrub process CPU/IO so we don't miss future occurrences.

anita: provider confirmed drive replacement ETA ~30h, vendor offered hot-swap but needs maintenance window. I'll sync with infra-scheduling.

hao: pushed systemd drop-in to gpu nodes, lowered concurrency. Observability: avgqu-sz dropped from ~22 to ~4 on test node, %util now ~45%.

maya: nice, pods recovering, one job restarted and completed.

jordan: follow-up: add a fleet-wide policy to pause vendor-initiated scrub if node has label 'gpu=true' and active GPU workloads. Add an alert when nvme util > 80% for > 2m.

liam: agree. Also let's add a playbook to throttle scrub via cgroup on any host where SMART triggers.

anita: will put maintenance and replacement ticket in calendar and notify affected customers.

maya: thanks team. I'll update the incident with mitigation steps and mark as partial containment.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-4839 status changed to "partial_containment" by maya at 1805123698.

jordan: postmortem action items: (1) autoscaler label policy, (2) scrub throttle runbook, (3) dashboard + alerting, (4) vendor replacement SLA review.

maya: adding to backlog and assigning owners. :white_check_mark:
